title: Sounds all around us
examples: Can you show me how sound travels?

explain.say: Sound is made when something shakes.
These quick shakes are called vibrations.
Some sounds are loud, and some are quiet.
Some sounds are high, like a tiny bell.
Some sounds are low, like a big truck.
When you clap your hands, they shake the air. The sound travels to your ears.

faq.q: How does sound get from one place to another?
faq.a: Sound travels as vibrations through the air, through water and through solid things.
asks: Does sound need air to move?

faq.a: No, vibrations can be very small making quiet sounds. Big vibrations make loud sounds.
asks: Does the size of the shake matter?

faq.q: What makes a high sound sound different?
faq.a: High sounds come from fast, small vibrations. Think of a tiny whistle making fast shakes.

faq.q: Can I make sound without shaking anything?
faq.a: No, all sounds we hear come from some kind of vibration. Something must shake to make sound.

faq.q: Is the loudness related to the strength of the shake?
faq.a: Yes, a stronger shake creates bigger vibrations, which makes a louder sound. A weak shake makes a quiet sound.
asks: Does strong shaking mean loud sound?

facts: Loudness is related to the size of the vibrations.
Pitch is related to how fast the vibrations are.

quiz.say: You pluck a guitar string. It shakes very fast. What is the shaking called?
quiz.why: A fast shake is a vibration. Vibrations make sound.

wrong.0: Pitch is how high or low a sound is.
wrong.2: A whisper is a quiet voice.

quiz.say: How does a whisper sound, next to a shout?
quiz.why: A whisper makes small vibrations, so it is quiet.

wrong.0: A shout is louder, and a whisper is soft.
wrong.1: High or low is about pitch, and this is about loudness.

quiz.say: Small things often shake very fast. What kind of sound do they make?
quiz.why: Fast shakes make high sounds, like a tiny bell.

wrong.1: Low sounds come from slow shakes, like a big drum.
wrong.2: Anything that shakes makes a sound.
